thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: High-severity alert - host node-aa-123 showing repeated GPU driver resets and container OOMs. Paging SRE rotation. PD: https://pd.example/incident/INC-7890 :rotating_light:

incident-bot: auto-attach: recent dmesg snippet, nv-host metrics, pod list

sara-oncall: I'm oncall. Seeing repeated 'Xid 79' style GPU errors, plus rapid oom kills in inference-worker pods on node-aa-123. Pod count on that host down from 12 -> 5 in last 7m.

sara-oncall: dmesg excerpt: ```
[ 2345.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=8743, Ch 00000001, not multi-process aware
[ 2345.123460] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 2345.123467] kernel: oom_kill_process: Killed process 8743 (inference-worker) total-vm: 123456kB
```

ben-runtime: thx sara. Can you confirm container logs? last 2 lines from pod inference-worker-7: ```
E tensorflow: Cuda error: out of memory
F inference: failed to allocate GPU buffer
```

ben-runtime: If it's GPU OOMs -> could be kernel/driver leak or ECC storm. Short term: cordon+drain node to stop scheduling more pods, and route new requests away from impacted pods.

maya-sre: Initiating cordon/drain now. 
`kubectl cordon node-aa-123`
`kubectl drain node-aa-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --force`

maya-sre: Starting eviction of noncritical pods to reduce pressure. Will scale up spare gpu nodes in the dedicated pool (autoscaler bounce).

chris-cust-success: Any customer impact yet? I'm seeing a spike in 504s for prod-embeddings—scoreboard shows ~2% error rate increased over last 6m. I'm preparing a short bridge message if it looks sustained.

kevin-support: Confirming customers A and B reported degraded embeddings. We opened interim support tickets. Can we enable fallback routing to smaller model-quantized variants while we stabilize?

lia-eng-runtime: I can flip the routing policy to prefer cpu-backed small-embed model for new requests and divert heavy batch jobs. Pushing config: `routing:update --service embeddings --fallback small-embed-v2`

lia-eng-runtime: Also did a soft restart of nvidia driver on the host to try to clear GPU state: `ssh node-aa-123 sudo systemctl restart nvidia-docker && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` — logs show driver restarted but dmesg still reports occasional Xid.

ops-bot: NOTE: Added tag `investigating:gpu-flare` to node-aa-123 and created infra task INFRA-3421 for kernel-level trace collection.

sara-oncall: Node still flapping after driver restart. Isolated to GPU slot 0 (phys 65:00) per `nvidia-smi -q` output. I'm marking node-aa-123 unschedulable and letting drain finish. Pods are coming back on other nodes but some large-batch workers are pending until new capacity spins up.

ben-runtime: On the runtime side, let's proactively reduce memory working sets: apply config patch to inference-worker: set --max-batch-size=8 and --kv-cache-lifetime=60s to lower GPU footprint while we rotate nodes.

ben-runtime: Patch command: `kubectl set env deploy/inference-worker MAX_BATCH=8 KV_CACHE_TTL=60` — rolling restart in progress.

chris-cust-success: I've sent a short customer notice: "We're aware of elevated errors for embeddings; traffic is being routed to a fallback model while we investigate. We'll update within 60 minutes."

kevin-support: Customer bridge open: https://zoom/bridge/12345. Attendees: ops, runtime, cs.

maya-sre: For immediate reduction of noise, I'm removing the node from the servicing pool and performing a hardware-level power-cycle on the server (coordinating with colo). If that doesn't stabilize, we'll isolate the GPU and mark node for deep forensic/replace.

lia-eng-runtime: For telemetry: collecting `nvidia-smi -q`, `dmesg -T`, container coredumps, and driver logs. Uploading to secure bucket for postmortem: s3://redwood-incident/INC-7890/artifacts

incident-bot: Created incident ticket INC-7890 (sev 2). Playbook: GPU-driver-reset -> isolate node -> route fallback -> collect artifacts.

sara-oncall: Current status: cordon+drain complete. 10 pods evicted, 8 rescheduled on healthy GPU nodes, 2 pending due to capacity. Fallback routing in place; error rate for embeddings down to 0.6%.

ben-runtime: Next steps: if we see another Xid within 30m, isolate the physical GPU (remove from driver via device-plugin or set KUBE_TAINT to quiesce), and replace node. Also enable kernel param to reduce ECC flood logging: `echo 1 > /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/disable_ecc_emergency` (ops only, risk-aware).

maya-sre: Agreed. For now we'll keep the node drained and let autoscaler create new nodes. Schedule oncall follow-up in 3h to review telemetry and decide on repro or hardware swap.

chris-cust-success: I'll coordinate post-incident customer follow-up and include timeline + mitigations.

sara-oncall: Thanks team. Tagging in the follow-up checklist: collect logs, confirm customer impact list, confirm replacement plan if recurrence. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Auto-note: runbook step completed: drain -> fallback routing -> artifact collection.

maya-sre: Closing live paging thread; keeping incident ticket open for postmortem. If anything spikes, reopen thread.
